checklist.step: Fix the advice scope and the governing jurisdiction before opening a fact-find
actions: In Salesforce FSC create the Opportunity and set Advice Basis to Advised or Non-Advised — a non-advised execution-only sale takes a different, shorter data set and must not use the advised path.
Set Customer Country of Residence, Country of Citizenship and Place of Solicitation on the Account; these three fields drive which jurisdiction overlay the Fact Find record applies.

Open the jurisdiction overlay matrix on the Fact Find record and read out the mandatory data items for that country and product family (for example NAIC Model 275 Section 6.A items for a US annuity, IDD Art. 20 demands-and-needs for an EEA sale).
Where residence and solicitation country differ, email Regulatory Counsel for the applicable-law call before any data is collected and paste the answer into the Advice Basis Notes field.
checklist.done: the Opportunity shows advice basis, all three country fields and a named jurisdiction overlay, with counsel's applicable-law note attached for any cross-border case.

checklist.step: Confirm the producer may lawfully solicit this customer before collecting data
actions: For US business, run a Producer Database inquiry in NIPR Gateway on the writing producer's NPN and confirm an active resident or non-resident licence plus a live appointment with the writing company in the solicitation state.
For EEA business, look the intermediary up on the home-state register published under IDD Art. 3 and confirm the passporting notification covers the customer's country.
Compare the licence lines of authority to the product family — a life-only licence cannot support a variable annuity recommendation.
Write the NPN or register number, licence expiry and appointment date onto the Opportunity and block the Fact Find record if any is missing or expired.
checklist.done: an active licence, an appointment or passport covering the customer's jurisdiction, and the correct line of authority are recorded against the Opportunity.

checklist.step: Capture and verify the customer's identity to CDD standard
actions: Collect on the Fact Find: full legal name, date of birth, residential address, nationality, national identifier and occupation, and for entity owners the legal form, registration number and registered address.
Obtain a government-issued photographic identity document plus one address proof dated within three months, and record the document type, number, issuing country and expiry.
Identify and record every beneficial owner holding 25% or more of a corporate or trust policyowner, and the intended policy beneficiaries, as required by ICP 22 and FATF Recommendation 10.
Run the identity through the screening platform and attach the verification result reference to the Fact Find record.
Reject a recommendation path outright where identity cannot be verified and hand the case to the Financial Crime AML Officer instead of proceeding on partial data.
checklist.done: verified identity documents, beneficial owners and beneficiaries are recorded with a screening reference on the Fact Find record.

checklist.step: Screen the parties and set the ML/TF risk tier that governs how much profile is required
actions: Screen policyowner, insured, payer and beneficiaries against the sanctions, PEP and adverse-media lists in the AML platform and clear or escalate each hit in the alert queue with a written disposition.

Score the four ICP 22.3 risk dimensions on the risk-tier form — customer (PEP, non-resident, complex ownership), product (single-premium, high cash value, assignable), channel (face-to-face, digital, third-party introducer) and geography (FATF grey/black list, high-corruption index).
Set the tier to Simplified, Standard or Enhanced and write the tier plus the driving dimension back to the Salesforce FSC Fact Find record.
For Enhanced, record the additional requirements now due: source of wealth narrative, senior-management approval to onboard, and an ongoing-monitoring review date 12 months out.
Never let a Simplified tier be applied to a customer resident in a FATF-listed jurisdiction — that combination is blocked and must be reasoned by the Financial Crime AML Officer if overridden.
checklist.done: every party is screened and dispositioned, and a documented risk tier with its driving dimension sits on the Fact Find record.

checklist.step: Capture the customer's financial situation with tested figures, not estimates
actions: Enter on the Financial Goals object: annual household income and its source, annual outgoings, total net worth, liquid net worth, existing debts and any expected material change in income within five years.
Enter the tax situation — marginal rate, tax residence, and any reporting status (FATCA/CRS self-certification reference) that affects product choice.
Compute and record the proportion of liquid net worth the proposed premium would consume; flag the case for the Annuity Suitability Analyst where it exceeds the product family's liquidity limit.
Where figures are supplied verbally, read them back to the customer and record the read-back date and time in the Fact Find audit note.
checklist.done: income, outgoings, net worth, liquid net worth, debts and tax residence are recorded with a premium-to-liquid-net-worth ratio computed.

checklist.step: Record the customer's needs, objectives and time horizon in their own terms
actions: Record the demands and needs statement required by IDD Art. 20(1) as a free-text narrative in the customer's own words — protection, income in retirement, estate transfer, debt cover — not a picked-list code alone.
Enter the intended time horizon in years, the earliest date funds may be needed, and whether the customer expects to make withdrawals during any surrender-charge period.
Record dependants, their ages and any special-needs beneficiary, since these change the appropriate death benefit and settlement option.
Where the stated horizon is shorter than the product's surrender-charge schedule, raise the mismatch on the record now rather than at the suitability review.
checklist.done: a narrative demands-and-needs statement, a time horizon in years and dependants are recorded, with any horizon-to-surrender-period mismatch flagged.

checklist.step: Capture risk tolerance, financial experience and financial capacity to bear loss
actions: Administer the risk-tolerance questionnaire on the Fact Find record and store the individual answers, not only the summary score, so the score can be re-derived later.
Record prior experience with each relevant instrument type — mutual funds, variable products, indexed products, structured notes — with an approximate holding period for each.
Record capacity for loss separately from appetite: the maximum reduction in the invested amount the customer could absorb without changing their standard of living.
Reconcile the tolerance score to the stated objectives and note any contradiction (for example a lowest-tolerance answer set alongside an equity-linked objective) for the reviewer to resolve.
checklist.done: individual questionnaire answers, a derived tolerance score, product experience and a stated capacity for loss are on the record, with contradictions flagged.

checklist.step: Inventory existing coverage and identify any replacement or surrender
actions: List every existing life, annuity and long-term-care contract the customer holds: carrier, contract number, issue date, current cash value, death benefit, remaining surrender charge and any living benefit rider.
Search the group's own policy administration system on the customer's name and national identifier to find in-force contracts the customer forgot to mention.

Where any existing contract would be surrendered, exchanged or reduced, set the Replacement flag and capture the surrender charge amount, lost rider value and any new contestability or suicide-clause period that restarts.
Count exchanges in the last 60 months and flag churning risk to the Annuity Suitability Analyst where more than one appears.
Attach the customer's most recent statement for each replaced contract to the Fact Find record.
checklist.done: existing coverage is inventoried against the admin system, and any replacement carries surrender cost, lost benefits and a 60-month exchange count.

checklist.step: Obtain source of funds and source of wealth where the risk tier demands it
actions: For every sale, record the source of the premium: salary, pension lump sum, property sale, inheritance, business proceeds, or transfer from a named existing contract, plus the paying institution and account country.

For Enhanced-tier cases, additionally document source of wealth as a narrative covering how the customer's overall wealth was accumulated, corroborated by at least one independent document (audited accounts, sale contract, probate grant, tax return).
Refuse third-party premium payment unless the payer relationship is documented and approved by the Financial Crime AML Officer.
Compare the premium against declared income and net worth and raise an alert in the AML platform where the premium is disproportionate to the declared means.
File corroborating documents to the case and record the document type and date on the Fact Find record.
checklist.done: premium source is recorded for every sale and Enhanced-tier cases carry a corroborated source-of-wealth narrative with a proportionality check.

checklist.step: Screen for vulnerability, capacity and the need for a trusted contact
actions: Work the vulnerability indicators on the Fact Find record — age band, recent bereavement, serious illness, cognitive difficulty, low financial literacy, language other than the sales language.
Where an indicator is present, record the adjustment made: extended decision time, a second contact, plain-language materials, or a translated illustration.
Offer and record a trusted contact person (name, relationship, contact details) for older customers, and record the customer's refusal where declined.
Escalate any doubt about mental capacity to the Distribution Operations Manager and pause the sale rather than proceeding to a recommendation.
checklist.done: vulnerability indicators are worked, adjustments recorded, and a trusted contact is captured or an explicit refusal is logged.

checklist.step: Handle a customer refusal to provide required profile information
actions: Record each refused item individually on the Fact Find record with the date and the customer's stated reason — never leave the field blank as though unasked.
Explain and log that the group cannot make a recommendation without the item, and offer the non-advised execution-only route where the local overlay permits it.
Where a CDD item is refused, stop the sale outright and refer to the Financial Crime AML Officer for a suspicious-activity assessment; a CDD refusal is not a route to execution-only.
Obtain the customer's signed acknowledgement that a refusal narrows what may be offered and file it with the profile.
checklist.done: each refused item is logged with reason and consequence, and CDD refusals are referred to Financial Crime rather than worked around.

checklist.step: Run the pre-recommendation completeness gate
actions: Trigger the Fact Find completeness validation, which blocks the Recommendation record from being created while any mandatory item for the jurisdiction overlay is empty.
Check the profile date is on or before today and no more than 90 days old; where older, send it back to the producer for refresh instead of overriding.
Confirm the risk tier is populated and, for Enhanced, that senior-management onboarding approval is attached.
Where a gate override is genuinely needed, require a written business reason plus Head of Compliance approval recorded on the Opportunity, and count the override in the monthly conduct metrics.
Release the Recommendation record only once the gate passes.
checklist.done: the recommendation record cannot open until the gate passes, and every override carries a written reason and Head of Compliance approval.

checklist.step: Have the customer confirm the profile before it is used
actions: Generate the profile summary document from Salesforce FSC and send it for signature through DocuSign to the customer's verified email or postal address.
Ask the customer to correct anything wrong before signing, and re-issue rather than annotate where a correction is made.

Capture the DocuSign envelope id, the completion timestamp and the signer IP or authentication method onto the Fact Find record — the timestamp is the evidence that the profile pre-dates the recommendation.
Give the customer a copy of the signed profile in the same session and record delivery.
checklist.done: a customer-signed profile exists with a DocuSign envelope id and a completion timestamp earlier than the recommendation date.

checklist.step: Archive the profile and bind it to the application record
actions: File the signed profile, identity and source-of-funds documents and the risk-tier decision into the repository indexed by application number, customer identifier, producer NPN and jurisdiction.
Apply the retention label of 10 years from policy termination so the record survives surrender and death claims.
Write the repository document id back onto the policy record in the administration system so underwriting and any later complaint handler can retrieve it in one hop.
Confirm the repository search returns the profile on a search by application number and by producer NPN.
checklist.done: the profile set is filed, retention-labelled, cross-linked to the policy record and retrievable by application number and producer.

checklist.step: Refresh profiles that go stale on in-force and repeat business
actions: Run the monthly stale-profile report listing customers with an open opportunity, an Enhanced-tier ongoing-monitoring review date now due, or a profile older than 12 months where a further recommendation is planned.
Issue refresh tasks to the writing producer with a 30-day due date and copy the servicing agency principal.
Re-run screening on refresh and re-derive the risk tier — a change in residence country or a new PEP status must move the tier before any further sale.
Report unrefreshed cases past 30 days to the Distribution Operations Manager for producer-level follow-up.
checklist.done: stale and monitoring-due profiles are identified monthly, refresh tasks are issued with a 30-day deadline and overdue cases are escalated.

testing.step: Build the population of advised sales made in the quarter
actions: Extract every Opportunity with Advice Basis = Advised and a recommendation date inside the quarter, with customer jurisdiction, product family, producer NPN, risk tier and premium.
Add applications taken through the bancassurance and broker portals so channels outside the direct sales force cannot fall out of scope.
Stratify the population by jurisdiction overlay and by risk tier, and record the counts per stratum in the workpaper.
testing.done: a stratified population of advised sales for the quarter exists with counts by jurisdiction and risk tier.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to policies actually issued
actions: Extract all life and annuity policies issued in the quarter from the administration system and match to the Salesforce FSC population on application number.
Investigate every issued policy with no matching advised opportunity — these are the sales most likely to carry no profile at all.
Investigate the reverse direction too: recommendations with no issued policy, to confirm they were declined rather than issued under a different application number.
Resolve or list every unmatched record before drawing the sample and record the reconciliation in the workpaper.
testing.done: issued policies and advised opportunities are reconciled both ways, with every difference explained or carried as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of Enhanced-risk-tier sales and 100% of sales to customers resident in FATF grey- or black-listed jurisdictions.
Take 30 further records at random using a recorded seed, allocated across jurisdictions in proportion to population, with a minimum of 5 per jurisdiction that has any activity.
Add a judgemental block of sales by producers who appear in the top decile for premium-to-declared-income ratio.
Record the seed, population size, stratum counts and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible from a recorded seed, and covers all enhanced-tier and high-risk-geography sales.

testing.step: Re-perform the completeness assessment against the jurisdiction overlay
actions: Open each sampled Fact Find record and, without reading the gate result, work the mandatory item list for that jurisdiction overlay yourself, item by item.
Score each item present / absent / present-but-unusable (for example net worth entered as a round zero, or objectives entered as a single word).
Compare your conclusion to the recorded gate pass and treat a gate pass over a blank or unusable mandatory item as an exception.
Capture the Fact Find screen showing the disputed items into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled record has an independent completeness conclusion and a captured screen for every disputed item.

testing.step: Prove the profile pre-dates the recommendation
actions: Pull the DocuSign envelope completion timestamp for each sampled profile and the recommendation creation timestamp from Salesforce FSC.
Compute recommendation date minus profile signature date for every sampled record; any negative value is an automatic fail regardless of content quality.
Compute profile age at application and list every record over the 90-day staleness limit.
Confirm any record with a negative or over-age result carries the written override reason and Head of Compliance approval the procedure requires.
testing.done: the date arithmetic is recomputed for every sampled record and each back-dated or stale profile is listed with its override status.

testing.step: Re-perform the ML/TF risk tiering
actions: For each sampled record, re-score the four ICP 22.3 dimensions from the underlying customer, product, channel and geography data and reach an independent tier.
Compare to the recorded tier; a tier set lower than your own conclusion is an exception even where the sale itself was unremarkable.
For Enhanced-tier cases, confirm the source-of-wealth narrative is corroborated by an independent document and that senior-management onboarding approval is attached and dated before issue.
Re-run screening on the sampled parties against today's list and note any hit that existed at the time of sale but was not dispositioned.
testing.done: each sampled tier is independently re-derived and every under-tiered or uncorroborated enhanced case is listed.

testing.step: Trace the profile to retained evidence and to the identifiers on the policy
actions: Search the repository by application number for each sampled record and confirm the signed profile, identity documents and source-of-funds evidence are all present.
Confirm the repository document id is written back onto the policy record and that the retention label reads 10 years from termination.
Confirm the producer NPN on the profile matches the NPN credited on the policy and on the commission record — a mismatch signals a sale written by someone other than the profile taker.
List records where evidence exists in Salesforce FSC but was never archived, since those will not survive a regulator request.
testing.done: every sampled profile is located in the repository, correctly labelled, and its producer identifier agrees with the policy and commission records.

testing.step: Test the refusal, vulnerability and override handling
actions: Extract all records in the quarter with a logged refusal, a vulnerability indicator or a completeness-gate override and take the whole set where it is under 25, otherwise sample 25.
Confirm each refusal names the item and the reason and that an advised recommendation did not follow a CDD refusal.
Confirm each vulnerability indicator has a recorded adjustment and that the sale was not concluded in the same session where extended decision time was recorded as the adjustment.
Confirm every override carries a written business reason and Head of Compliance approval dated before issue, and count overrides by producer to find repeat users.
testing.done: refusals, vulnerability adjustments and overrides are each verified against the procedure and repeat override users are named.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception carrying application number, jurisdiction, producer NPN, the failed item and the customer-harm assessment.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — gate overridden, profile back-dated, item unusable, tier under-set, evidence never archived — and name an owner in Distribution.
Set a remediation date inside 30 days and, where the customer may have been sold an unsuitable contract, open a customer-outcome review including free-look or rescission options.
Refer any enhanced-tier source-of-funds gap to Financial Crime for a suspicious-activity decision within one business day.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a 30-day remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the completeness pass rate and compare it to the 98% threshold, and state separately whether any enhanced-tier source-of-funds instance occurred.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each supporting finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Distribution and gated none of the sampled profiles, sign the workpaper.
Report the result, the producer-level outliers and any customer-outcome reviews to the Conduct Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, the pass rate against the 98% threshold and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Receive the case at the desk and confirm it is reviewable
actions: Take the next case from the suitability queue sorted by desk age and open the linked Salesforce FSC recommendation and Fact Find records.

Confirm the mandatory pack is attached: signed customer profile, product illustration with its version and run date, application, replacement forms where flagged, and the producer's written rationale.
Return the case to the producer as Incomplete — not Declined — where any pack item is missing, naming each missing item and starting the 10-business-day cure clock.
Start the 2-business-day decision SLA timer and record the reviewer name so the case cannot later be decided by the producer's own manager.
checklist.done: the case has a complete pack, a named reviewer who is not in the producer's reporting line, and a running decision SLA.

checklist.step: Test the recommended product against the recorded need
actions: Read the demands-and-needs narrative from the Fact Find and write, in your own words on the scoring sheet, what the customer said they were trying to achieve.
Map each recommended contract feature and rider to a specific stated need — a guaranteed lifetime withdrawal rider must trace to a stated income need, not to a general preference for guarantees.
Score any feature that maps to no stated need as unjustified and require the producer to either evidence the need or remove the feature.
Confirm a simpler or cheaper contract in the same product family would not meet the same need, and record why it was rejected.
checklist.done: every recommended feature and rider traces to a stated need and the rejection of a simpler alternative is reasoned on the scoring sheet.

checklist.step: Test time horizon and liquidity against the surrender-charge schedule
actions: Read the surrender-charge schedule from the illustration — first-year percentage, duration in years, and the free-withdrawal allowance per year.

Compare the schedule duration to the customer's stated time horizon and to the earliest date funds may be needed; a horizon shorter than the schedule is a mandatory decline trigger unless the free-withdrawal allowance genuinely covers the stated need.
Compute premium as a percentage of liquid net worth and compare to the product family's liquidity limit recorded in the procedure.
Confirm the customer retains an emergency reserve after the premium and record the reserve figure on the scoring sheet.
checklist.done: the surrender schedule, horizon, premium-to-liquid-net-worth percentage and remaining emergency reserve are recorded and tested against the stated limits.

checklist.step: Test the recommendation against risk tolerance and capacity for loss
actions: Re-derive the tolerance score from the stored individual questionnaire answers rather than accepting the summary figure.
Compare the contract's downside profile — index participation caps and floors, subaccount volatility, guarantee strength — to the derived tolerance band and to the stated capacity for loss.
For variable and indexed contracts, confirm the customer's recorded product experience covers the instrument type or that additional explanation was given and evidenced.
Record any tolerance-to-product mismatch as a query to the producer with the specific answer that drove it.
checklist.done: the tolerance score is re-derived from raw answers and the contract's downside profile sits inside the derived band and the stated capacity for loss.

checklist.step: Run the replacement and exchange economics where a contract is being surrendered
actions: Open the replacement comparison workbook and enter for the existing contract: cash value, surrender charge, remaining charge years, guaranteed rate, living or death benefit rider value, and any bonus subject to recapture.
Enter the same fields for the proposed contract, including new surrender-charge duration, any premium bonus and its vesting schedule.
Compute the break-even year — the point at which the proposed contract recovers the surrender charge and lost rider value — and record it on the scoring sheet.
Decline where the break-even year exceeds the customer's stated horizon, or where a valuable guaranteed benefit is being abandoned without a compensating stated need.
Confirm the state or local replacement notice and comparison statement were delivered and signed on or before the application date.
checklist.done: a computed break-even year, the abandoned guarantees and a signed replacement notice are on file, and the break-even sits inside the customer's stated horizon.

checklist.step: Verify the illustration used to sell the contract
actions: Check the illustration version and run date against the currently approved version list and reject any illustration run on a superseded version.
Confirm the illustration inputs — age, sex where permitted, premium, rider elections, index allocation — match the application exactly, field by field.
Confirm non-guaranteed elements are shown alongside guaranteed elements and that no hypothetical rate above the approved maximum was illustrated.
Confirm the customer-signed illustration copy is on file with the same version identifier as the one reviewed.
checklist.done: the illustration is a current approved version, its inputs match the application field by field, and a signed copy with the same version identifier is on file.

checklist.step: Confirm the customer sits inside the product's defined target market
actions: Open the product's target market statement produced by the product oversight and governance process and read its positive and negative market criteria.
Test the customer against each criterion — age band, wealth band, objective type, horizon, distribution channel permitted — and record pass or fail per criterion.
Where the customer falls in a negative target market, decline the recommendation and record the criterion breached; a distribution override is not available.
Feed every out-of-target sale attempt back to the product committee as distribution feedback, since repeated attempts signal a mis-set target market or a mis-briefed channel.
checklist.done: the customer is tested against each target-market criterion with a recorded result, and negative-market cases are declined and fed back to the product committee.

checklist.step: Test cost and value, including compensation neutrality
actions: List the total cost of the recommended contract: mortality and expense charge, administrative fee, rider charges, fund expense ratios and any advisory fee, expressed as an annual percentage.
Compare that total to the cost of the two nearest alternatives on the approved shelf that would meet the same need and record the comparison.

Pull the first-year commission percentage payable on the recommendation and on each alternative from the commission platform, and check whether the recommended contract is also the highest-paying option.
Where the highest-paying option was recommended, require an explicit written justification from the producer and record whether it withstands the cost comparison.
Record any non-cash incentive, contest qualification or override that could have influenced the recommendation.
checklist.done: total annual cost is compared against two alternatives, the commission differential is recorded, and any highest-paying recommendation carries a tested written justification.

checklist.step: Check the producer's written rationale actually reasons the choice
actions: Read the producer's rationale and test it against three questions: does it name the customer's need, does it explain why this contract meets it, and does it explain why the alternatives were rejected.
Reject template language that would read identically for any customer — a rationale that never mentions this customer's figures is not a rationale.
Where the rationale contradicts the Fact Find (for example claims a long horizon where the profile records five years), query rather than reconcile it yourself.
Record the accepted rationale text into the scoring sheet so the decision file stands alone without the producer's system.
checklist.done: the rationale names the customer's own figures, reasons the choice and the rejection of alternatives, and is copied into the decision file.

checklist.step: Record the approve, query or decline decision
actions: Set the decision to Approve, Query or Decline with the reviewer name and a timestamp that the case system writes, not one the reviewer types.
For Approve, record every criterion that passed and any residual concern accepted, so a later reader sees the judgement rather than a tick.
For Query, list the specific items the producer must supply or correct and set the 10-business-day cure clock with auto-decline at expiry.
For Decline, name the decline trigger and notify the producer and the agency principal the same day.
Write the approval flag back to the policy administration system so issue is blocked until it is set.
checklist.done: a system-timestamped decision with a named reviewer and reasons exists, and the administration system holds the matching issue gate flag.

checklist.step: Work the query-and-cure loop without letting the case drift
actions: Send the query list to the producer through the case system, copying the agency principal, and record the send timestamp.
Chase at day 5 and warn that auto-decline falls at day 10; a cure supplied after issue is not a cure.
On receipt, route the cure back to the same reviewer rather than a fresh one, so the second look tests the same concern.
Where the cure changes the recommendation itself, restart the review from the need-match step rather than approving the amendment in isolation.
checklist.done: every query is tracked with send, chase and cure timestamps, routed back to the original reviewer, and auto-declines at day 10 if uncured.

checklist.step: Handle a declined case and any attempt to overturn it
actions: Take every request from distribution management to overturn a decline and require it in writing with the new evidence relied on.
Re-test the decline trigger yourself against the new evidence; an overturn on the same evidence the reviewer already saw is not permitted.
Record the overturn decision, the evidence and your name in the GRC platform and count the overturn in the monthly conduct metrics by product and by requesting manager.
Report any manager with more than two overturn requests in a quarter to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every overturn request is written, re-tested against the trigger, logged with the approver's name, and counted by requesting manager.

checklist.step: Give the customer the outcome and preserve the cooling-off route
actions: On approval and issue, send the customer the suitability statement summarising the need, the recommendation and the reason, alongside the contract.
State the free-look or cooling-off period that applies in the customer's jurisdiction, its length in days and the date it expires, and record that date on the policy record.
Record the contract delivery date and delivery method, since the free-look clock runs from delivery in most jurisdictions.
Route any customer objection raised in the free-look window to the Complaints Manager rather than to the writing producer.
checklist.done: the customer holds a suitability statement and a dated free-look expiry, and the delivery date is recorded on the policy.

checklist.step: Feed reviewer findings back into producer supervision
actions: Publish the monthly desk dashboard by producer: cases submitted, query rate, decline rate, top three decline triggers and average cure time.
Place any producer above twice the channel average decline rate onto heightened supervision — 100% pre-issue review plus a coaching session within 15 business days.
Send the top decline triggers to the Learning & Development Specialist so the next training cycle targets the actual failure modes rather than generic content.
Report producers who submit repeated out-of-target-market recommendations to the Head of Distribution for channel action.
checklist.done: a per-producer desk dashboard is published monthly and outlier producers are on heightened supervision with a dated coaching session.

checklist.step: Archive the decision file for the retention period
actions: File the scoring sheet, replacement comparison workbook, illustration reviewed, producer rationale and dated decision into the repository indexed by policy number, producer NPN and reviewer.
Apply the 10-years-from-termination retention label and mark files under complaint or litigation hold as non-purgeable.
Confirm retrieval works by policy number, by reviewer and by decline trigger, since exam requests arrive in all three shapes.
Reconcile the archived file count to the desk decision count each month and chase any decision with no archived file.
checklist.done: every decision has an archived, retention-labelled file retrievable by policy, reviewer and decline trigger, reconciled monthly to the decision count.

testing.step: Build the population of recommendations and issued policies
actions: Extract every suitability desk case decided in the quarter with product family, producer NPN, reviewer, decision, decision timestamp and desk age.
Extract every life and annuity policy issued in the quarter from the administration system with its application number.
Join the two on application number and stratify by product family, replacement flag and reviewer.
testing.done: a joined population of desk decisions and issued policies exists, stratified by product family, replacement flag and reviewer.

testing.step: Reconcile issued policies to recorded approvals
actions: List every issued policy with no desk decision, with a Query decision, or with a Decline decision — each is an automatic exception with no judgement applied.
For each, read the issue timestamp against the decision timestamp and list any policy issued before its approval was recorded.
Check whether the administration system's issue gate flag was set manually rather than written by the case system, since a manual set defeats the control.
Resolve or list every difference before drawing the sample.
testing.done: every issued policy is matched to a pre-dated approval or listed as an exception, and manually set gate flags are identified.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of replacement and exchange sales and 100% of cases decided by any reviewer who had an exception in the prior quarter.
Take 30 approvals at random from the remainder using a recorded seed, allocated across product families in proportion to population.
Add a judgemental block of the ten largest premiums and the ten cases with the shortest desk age, since speed and size both correlate with cursory review.
Record the seed, stratum counts and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers all replacements, repeat-exception reviewers and the largest and fastest cases.

testing.step: Re-perform the best-interest decision on the same evidence
actions: Work each sampled case from the profile, illustration and application alone, completing a blank scoring sheet before opening the reviewer's sheet.
Reach your own approve or decline conclusion, then compare; a different conclusion, or the same conclusion reached on a criterion the reviewer never tested, is an exception.
Test specifically whether any mandatory decline trigger was present and approved over — horizon shorter than the surrender schedule, negative target market, break-even beyond horizon.
Record your reasoning per criterion so the difference can be discussed on substance rather than on judgement generally.
testing.done: each sampled case carries an independent scoring sheet completed before the reviewer's sheet was opened, with per-criterion reasoning.

testing.step: Recompute the replacement break-even and surrender economics
actions: Rebuild the break-even calculation independently for every sampled replacement from the source contract statements rather than from the reviewer's workbook.
Recompute surrender charge, lost rider value, bonus recapture and the new surrender-charge duration, and compare the break-even year to the reviewer's figure.
Compare the recomputed break-even to the customer's stated horizon and list every case where it exceeds the horizon.
Check the workbook formulas for hard-coded values overwriting a formula, a common source of favourable break-even results.
testing.done: every sampled replacement has an independently rebuilt break-even, compared to both the reviewer's figure and the customer's horizon.

testing.step: Verify the illustration and application inputs agree
actions: For each sampled case, compare the signed illustration's version identifier to the approved version list as it stood on the run date.
Compare illustration inputs to the application field by field — age, premium, rider elections, index allocation — and list any difference however small.
Confirm no illustrated non-guaranteed rate exceeds the approved maximum for that product and run date.
Capture the illustration cover page and the application page into the workpaper for every difference found.
testing.done: illustration version and inputs are checked against the approved list and the application for every sampled case, with captures for each difference.

testing.step: Test target-market conformity and compensation neutrality
actions: Re-test each sampled customer against the product's target market statement criterion by criterion and list every approval of a negative-market customer.
Pull the first-year commission actually paid on each sampled sale and on the nearest approved alternatives, and recompute the differential.
Compute, across the sample, the proportion of approvals landing on the highest-paying available option and compare it to the proportion expected if compensation were neutral.
List any producer whose sampled recommendations sit exclusively on the highest-paying option for referral to Distribution Compliance.
testing.done: target-market conformity is re-tested per criterion and the highest-paying-option rate is computed for the sample and per producer.

testing.step: Test the query, decline and overturn population in full
actions: Take 100% of declines and overturns in the quarter rather than a sample, since the control's integrity lives here.
For each overturn, confirm written new evidence exists, that it is genuinely new, and that the Compliance Manager rather than distribution recorded the decision.
For each auto-decline at day 10, confirm no policy was subsequently issued on the same application number under a re-submitted case.
List any case re-submitted to a different reviewer after a decline — reviewer shopping is a control failure even where the second decision is defensible.
testing.done: all declines and overturns are tested, new evidence is verified, and any reviewer shopping or post-decline issue is listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and customer-outcome assessment
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with policy number, producer, reviewer, the criterion failed and an assessment of whether the customer is worse off.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — decline trigger overridden, break-even miscomputed, target market untested, rationale templated, issued without decision — and an owner.
Where the customer is worse off, open a redress assessment with Regulatory Counsel covering rescission, fee refund or contract replacement, with a 30-day decision date.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row and add the responsible reviewer to next quarter's 100% coverage list.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a customer-outcome assessment and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the re-performance agreement rate against the 95% threshold and state separately whether any approval over a mandatory decline trigger or any issue-without-decision occurred.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who decided none of the sampled cases and does not sit on the suitability desk, sign the workpaper.
Report the result, the overturn register and any redress assessments to the Conduct Risk Committee and the Board Risk Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an agreement rate against the 95% threshold, a stated conclusion and a board committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the pre-solicitation training gate for every producer, broker and bancassurance adviser distributing group products; escalates unqualified-solicitation findings to the Head of Distribution and the Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 19 Standard 19.3 (product oversight and governance, distribution to the identified target market) and Standard 19.8 read against the current ICP text, together with the distributor-competence rules that enforce them locally: NAIC Model 275 Section 7 product-specific and four-hour annuity training, EU IDD Art. 10 and Annex I minimum 15 hours annual professional training, Commission Delegated Regulation 2017/2358 Art. 10 distributor arrangements, FCA SYSC 5.1 and TC competence rules

In-scope processes.value: Producer onboarding and ongoing distribution enablement: carrier product training assignment on every product and rider launch or material change, jurisdiction-mandated annuity and suitability training, continuing professional development hours, and the solicitation entitlement gate that switches a producer's ability to quote a given product on or off

In-scope systems.value: Cornerstone LMS holds the training curricula, completion records and assessment scores; completions feed nightly into the agency/producer management system, which sets the per-product solicitation entitlement used by the quoting portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: Distributor Training and Solicitation Entitlement Procedure — curriculum design from the product oversight pack, jurisdiction training matrix, assessment pass mark of 80%, entitlement switch-on and switch-off rules, and the 30-day grace rule for material product changes

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Head of Distribution and endorsed by the Product Oversight Committee; the jurisdiction training matrix is re-approved annually and within 30 days of any change to a local producer training requirement

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Training must be completed before the first solicitation of a product — never after; new-product curricula must be published at least 15 business days before launch; material product changes carry a 30-day completion window after which entitlement is withdrawn automatically; jurisdiction CPD hours are tracked against each producer's licence renewal date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Cornerstone LMS reminders at 21, 10 and 3 days before a curriculum due date, plus a withdrawal-warning notice on day 25 of a 30-day change window; the agency/producer management system emails agency principals a weekly roster of producers due to lose entitlement

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Course version, completion date and time, assessment score and attempt count, plus the dated entitlement switch record, retained 7 years from the producer's termination of appointment and for the life of any market conduct examination covering the period

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any quote, application or issued policy written by a producer without the product entitlement is logged as an unqualified-solicitation exception with producer, agency, product, jurisdiction, policy count and remediation, including whether affected customers were contacted

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every unqualified-solicitation exception, including any decision to let affected policies stand, and approves reinstatement of a withdrawn entitlement

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every producer holding a live solicitation entitlement at quarter end, joined to the quarter's quotes, applications and issued policies by producer identifier and product, so that solicitation without entitlement surfaces at transaction level

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of sampled producers must hold a completed, in-date curriculum for every product they solicited; zero tolerance on an issued policy written without the product entitlement — any single instance fails the quarter and triggers a full-population sweep for that product

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The gate operates continuously at quote time, so an automated daily entitlement-versus-activity reconciliation runs against the prior day's quotes and this independent test runs quarterly, with 100% coverage of products launched or materially changed during the quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Distribution and Learning and Development and must not administer LMS records or entitlement switches

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Producer training roster by product and jurisdiction with completion dates and assessment scores, the curriculum content pack per product, and the entitlement change log, assembled for a market conduct examination producer-file request within 10 business days

checklist.step: Take the product oversight pack and turn it into a training specification
actions: Collect from the Product Oversight Committee the approved pack for the product: target market statement, negative target market, distribution strategy, key risks, charges and rider mechanics.

Write the training specification listing what a producer must be able to do after training — identify the target market, explain the surrender schedule, describe rider trade-offs, name the disclosures due.
State the permitted distribution channels and any channel the product must not be sold through, so the curriculum can be assigned by channel.
Hand the specification to the Instructional Designer at least 25 business days before launch so the course can be built and published 15 business days ahead.
checklist.done: an approved training specification with learning outcomes and permitted channels exists and is handed over on the 25-business-day lead time.

checklist.step: Build the course and its assessment in the LMS
actions: Create the course in Cornerstone LMS with a version number tied to the product's approved document set, so a later product change forces a new course version rather than an edit.

Build the assessment with at least 15 questions covering target market, surrender and withdrawal mechanics, rider trade-offs, replacement rules and mandatory disclosures, with an 80% pass mark and a maximum of three attempts.
Set the completion record to capture course version, start and completion timestamps, score and attempt count — a bare completion flag will not survive an examination.
Have the Compliance Analyst review the content against the approved product documents and record the review before publication.
checklist.done: a versioned course with a reviewed 15-question assessment, an 80% pass mark and timestamped completion capture is ready to publish.

checklist.step: Map the jurisdiction-mandated training on top of the carrier course
actions: Open the jurisdiction training matrix and, for each jurisdiction the product will be sold in, record the mandated pre-solicitation requirement — for US annuity states the one-time four-hour annuity course plus product-specific training, for EEA the IDD Art. 10 annual hours, for other markets the local competence rule.
Record which requirements must be satisfied by an approved external provider and which the carrier may deliver itself.
Create a curriculum per jurisdiction bundling the carrier course, the mandated external course and any refresher, with its own due date rule.
Flag jurisdictions where the mandated course must be completed before appointment rather than before solicitation, since the gate sits earlier there.
checklist.done: each selling jurisdiction has a curriculum bundling carrier and mandated external training, with the correct gate point recorded.

checklist.step: Assign curricula to the right producers by channel and appointment
actions: Extract from the producer management system every producer appointed or contracted for the product's jurisdictions, with channel, agency, licence lines and appointment date.
Exclude producers in channels the distribution strategy does not permit and record the exclusion so they are not later switched on by default.
Push the assignment into Cornerstone LMS keyed on the producer identifier used in both systems, and reconcile the assigned count to the extracted count the same day.
Send agency principals the roster of their assigned producers with the completion due date and the consequence of missing it.
checklist.done: every permitted-channel appointed producer holds an LMS assignment, the counts reconcile, and agency principals hold the roster and due date.

checklist.step: Verify externally delivered training rather than trusting the certificate
actions: For US annuity training, query the producer's continuing education transcript through NIPR Gateway or the state CE provider record and confirm the four-hour annuity course sits on the transcript with a completion date.
Compare the transcript completion date to the certificate the producer supplied and investigate any difference rather than filing both.
For EEA producers, obtain the home-state register entry or the intermediary's annual training declaration evidencing the 15-hour minimum.
Record the verification source, date and the verifier's name against the LMS record; a producer-supplied PDF alone is not verification.
Reject and re-request any certificate without a provider name, course code and completion date.
checklist.done: every externally delivered requirement is verified at source with the verification source, date and verifier recorded against the LMS record.

checklist.step: Run completions and chase the tail before launch
actions: Publish the curriculum 15 business days before launch and open the completion dashboard by agency and channel.
Send the automated reminders at 21, 10 and 3 days before the due date and add a personal chase from the Agency Relations Manager for agencies below 70% completion at day 10.
Review failed assessment attempts by question to spot content that is failing everyone, and fix the content rather than lowering the pass mark.
Publish a daily completion percentage to the Head of Distribution in the final week before launch.
checklist.done: the curriculum is live 15 business days before launch, reminders and agency-level chases have run, and daily completion reporting is in place.

checklist.step: Switch solicitation entitlement on only where the curriculum is complete
actions: Configure the nightly feed so a passed, in-date curriculum plus an active licence and appointment sets the per-product solicitation entitlement to Yes, and nothing else does.
Confirm the quoting portal reads the entitlement at quote time and returns a hard block, not a warning, when it is No.
Remove any manual entitlement override capability from agency and sales users, leaving it with the Producer Compliance Manager alone and logged.
Test the block before launch with a deliberately untrained test producer identifier and record the test result.
checklist.done: entitlement is set only by a passed curriculum plus active licence, the portal hard-blocks at quote time, and the block is evidenced by a recorded pre-launch test.

checklist.step: Withdraw entitlement automatically when training lapses or a product changes materially
actions: Set the rule that a licence expiry, appointment termination or lapsed refresher immediately drops the entitlement to No on the next nightly run.
On a material product change, issue the new course version and open a 30-day completion window; entitlement drops automatically for anyone incomplete on day 31.
Send a withdrawal-warning notice on day 25 to the producer and the agency principal naming the product and the withdrawal date.
Record every withdrawal and reinstatement in the entitlement change log with reason, actor and timestamp.
checklist.done: lapses and material changes drive automatic withdrawal with a day-25 warning, and every entitlement change is logged with reason and actor.

checklist.step: Reconcile yesterday's sales activity against entitlement every day
actions: Run the daily reconciliation joining the prior day's quotes, applications and issued policies to the entitlement table on producer identifier and product code.
List every transaction where entitlement was No or absent at the transaction timestamp — not at today's date, which would hide a later switch-on.
Route each hit to the Producer Compliance Manager the same morning with producer, agency, product, jurisdiction and premium.
Track the daily hit count as a control metric and treat a non-zero count on two consecutive days as a control failure rather than a data issue.
checklist.done: a daily entitlement-versus-activity reconciliation runs on transaction-time entitlement and every hit is routed the same morning.

checklist.step: Investigate and remediate an unqualified solicitation
actions: Open a GRC issue naming the producer, agency, product, jurisdiction, transaction dates and the number of affected customers.
Suspend the producer's entitlement across all products pending investigation and notify the agency principal in writing the same day.
Establish how the transaction passed the gate — portal bypass, manual override, stale entitlement feed, or a paper application routed outside the portal — and fix the route, not just the record.
Assess customer impact with the Annuity Suitability Analyst and decide whether affected customers must be contacted and offered a free-look extension or rescission.
Have the Head of Distribution sign the closure and any entitlement reinstatement.
checklist.done: each unqualified solicitation has a GRC issue, a suspended entitlement, an identified bypass route, a customer-impact decision and a signed closure.

checklist.step: Give distributors the product oversight information they must pass on
actions: Publish to the Broker and Agent Portal the target market statement, negative target market, distribution strategy and disclosure pack for each product, with a version and publication date.
Record each agency's acknowledgement of receipt, since the distributor arrangements rule expects the manufacturer to be able to show what was provided and when.
Re-issue and re-collect acknowledgements on every material product change, tied to the same 30-day window as the course.
Chase agencies with no acknowledgement at day 20 and escalate outstanding ones to the Head of Distribution at day 30.
checklist.done: every product's oversight pack is published with a version and date and every agency acknowledgement is recorded or escalated.

checklist.step: Track continuing professional development hours against licence renewal
actions: Load each producer's licence renewal date and jurisdiction CPD requirement into the producer management system.
Query CE transcripts through NIPR Gateway monthly for US producers and compare credited hours to the requirement, including any ethics-hour subcomponent.
Issue shortfall notices 90 days before renewal listing hours outstanding by category, and copy the agency principal at 45 days.
Drop entitlement on the day a licence lapses rather than waiting for the renewal outcome.
checklist.done: CPD hours are reconciled monthly against each producer's renewal date and shortfall notices are issued at 90 and 45 days.

checklist.step: Refresh curricula on a fixed cycle and after conduct findings
actions: Review every product curriculum annually against the current approved product documents and retire any course version referencing withdrawn documents.
Take the top decline triggers from the suitability desk and the top complaint root causes from the Complaints Manager and build them into the next course version.
Where a conduct finding names a specific failure mode, issue targeted remedial training to the affected producers with a 15-business-day due date rather than waiting for the annual cycle.
Record the evidence trail from finding to course change so the improvement loop is demonstrable.
checklist.done: curricula are reviewed annually, refreshed from suitability and complaint findings, and remedial training is issued within 15 business days of a conduct finding.

checklist.step: Publish the training and entitlement position to governance
actions: Publish the monthly distribution conduct pack: completion rates by product and agency, entitled producer counts, entitlement withdrawals, unqualified-solicitation count and open remediation.
Present the pack to the Product Oversight Committee alongside the sales-versus-target-market data, since training and target market fail together.
Escalate any product where completion is below 90% at launch plus 30 days as a distribution readiness issue.
Record the committee's decisions and any required distribution restriction in the minutes.
checklist.done: a monthly pack with completion, entitlement and unqualified-solicitation metrics is presented and minuted at the Product Oversight Committee.

checklist.step: Archive training and entitlement evidence for the retention period
actions: Export course versions, completion records with scores and attempt counts, external verification records and the entitlement change log into the repository monthly.
Index by producer identifier, product code, jurisdiction and date so an examiner's producer-file request can be answered without an LMS query.
Apply the 7-years-from-termination retention label and mark records inside an examination period as non-purgeable.
Reconcile the archived record count to the LMS completion count each month and chase differences.
checklist.done: training and entitlement evidence is archived monthly, indexed by producer and product, retention-labelled and reconciled to LMS counts.

testing.step: Build the entitled-producer population and join it to sales activity
actions: Extract every producer with a live solicitation entitlement at quarter end, by product code, jurisdiction, channel and agency.
Extract every quote, application and issued policy in the quarter with producer identifier, product code, jurisdiction and transaction timestamp.
Join the two on producer identifier and product code using entitlement as it stood at the transaction timestamp, not at extract date.
Record the population counts by product and channel in the workpaper.
testing.done: a joined population of entitlements and transactions exists, evaluated on transaction-time entitlement, with counts recorded by product and channel.

testing.step: Reconcile the entitlement roster to the LMS and licensing source records
actions: Match every entitled producer to a passed, in-date curriculum record in Cornerstone LMS and list entitlements with no supporting completion.
Match every entitled producer to an active licence and appointment in the producer management system and list entitlements sitting behind a lapsed licence.
Compare the LMS assigned count for each product to the appointed-producer count from the previous step and investigate any producer appointed but never assigned.
Resolve or list every difference before drawing the sample.
testing.done: the entitlement roster is reconciled to LMS completions and to licence status, with every unsupported entitlement listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of producers who sold a product launched or materially changed during the quarter, and 100% of producers whose entitlement was manually overridden.
Take 30 further producers at random from the entitled population using a recorded seed, allocated across channels in proportion to sales volume.
Add a judgemental block of the ten highest-volume producers, since a training gap there carries the largest customer population.
Record the seed, stratum counts and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers all new-product sellers, all manual overrides and the highest-volume producers.

testing.step: Re-perform the training verification at source for each sampled producer
actions: Open each sampled producer's LMS record and read course version, completion timestamp, assessment score and attempt count for every product they solicited.
Confirm the course version completed is the version current at the time of the first solicitation, not a superseded one.
Confirm the score meets the 80% pass mark and that attempts did not exceed three, and list any record showing a pass on a fourth attempt.
List any producer whose completion timestamp falls after their first quote or application for that product — the ordering is the whole control.
testing.done: each sampled producer's completion is verified for version, score, attempts and, critically, that it pre-dates their first solicitation.

testing.step: Verify externally mandated training independently of the producer's paperwork
actions: For each sampled US producer, query the CE transcript through NIPR Gateway and confirm the four-hour annuity course is credited with a date before first solicitation.
For each sampled EEA producer, obtain the register entry or annual training declaration evidencing the minimum annual hours.
Compare the source record to the certificate held on file and list every difference in provider, course code or completion date.
Capture the transcript or register screen into the workpaper for each sampled producer.
testing.done: every sampled producer's mandated external training is confirmed at the regulator or register source with a captured screen.

testing.step: Test the entitlement gate by attempting a blocked quote
actions: Using a controlled test producer identifier with entitlement set to No, attempt to build a quote for each product family in the portal.
Confirm the portal returns a hard block at the product selection step and does not allow the quote to be saved, printed or emailed.
Repeat through every alternate route — mobile quoting, agency bulk upload, telephone sales desk and paper application intake — since gates usually leak on the route nobody tests.
Record the route, the result and a screen capture for each attempt, and raise any route that permitted the quote as a control failure.
testing.done: the block is tested through every sales route with a recorded result and capture, and any permissive route is raised as a control failure.

testing.step: Test the daily reconciliation for completeness rather than trusting its zero
actions: Re-run the quarter's entitlement-versus-activity join yourself from raw extracts and compare your hit count to the daily reconciliation's reported hits.
Confirm the production reconciliation uses transaction-time entitlement; a join on current entitlement will under-report and must be listed as a design failure.
Confirm paper and telephone applications enter the reconciliation population, not only portal transactions.
List any day the reconciliation did not run and confirm the gap was investigated.
testing.done: an independent re-run of the join reconciles to the reported daily hits, with any design or coverage gap in the production reconciliation listed.

testing.step: Trace unqualified-solicitation findings through to customer outcome
actions: Take 100% of unqualified-solicitation issues raised in the quarter and read each investigation through to closure.
Confirm the bypass route was identified and fixed, and that the fix was tested rather than asserted.
Confirm a customer-impact assessment exists for every affected policy and that the free-look or rescission decision was made and communicated where the assessment required it.
Confirm the Head of Distribution signed each closure and each entitlement reinstatement, and list any reinstatement made before the curriculum was completed.
testing.done: every unqualified-solicitation issue is traced to a fixed bypass route, a customer-impact decision and a signed closure.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming producer, agency, product, jurisdiction, the number of transactions affected and the customer population involved.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — entitlement set without completion, completion after first solicitation, external training unverified, gate bypassed on an alternate route, withdrawal rule not applied — and an owner.
Set a 30-day remediation date, and where a product-wide gap is indicated, require a full-population sweep of that product before the date.
Carry every open exception into next quarter as a mandatory retest row and add the affected product to next quarter's 100% coverage list.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a 30-day remediation date and, where product-wide, a full-population sweep.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the sampled completion rate against the 100% requirement and, separately, the number of issued policies written without entitlement.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Distribution and Learning and Development and administers no LMS or entitlement records, sign the workpaper.

Report the result, the unqualified-solicitation count and any product sweeps to the Product Oversight Committee and the Conduct Risk Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating the completion rate, the unqualified-solicitation count, a conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.
