checklist.step: Maintain the disclosure matrix that drives everything downstream
actions: Maintain one row per jurisdiction, product family, channel and advice basis, listing every document due, its governing instrument, its timing point and the proof standard required.
Record for each document the current approved version number and effective date, and the date the underlying instrument was last checked.
Subscribe to the local regulator bulletin feeds for each jurisdiction and open a matrix change request within 5 business days of any instrument change.
Have Regulatory Counsel sign the matrix and each subsequent amendment before it goes live in the quoting and application systems.
checklist.done: a counsel-signed matrix names every required document, its timing point, proof standard and current version for every jurisdiction, product, channel and advice basis.

checklist.step: Serve the producer status, remuneration and conflicts disclosure first
actions: Before discussing any specific contract, serve the producer status disclosure naming the legal entity, its register or licence number, whether advice is given, and whether the producer represents one insurer, a limited panel or the whole market.
Serve the remuneration disclosure stating whether the producer is paid by commission, fee, another economic benefit or a combination, and where a fee is charged, the amount or its calculation basis.
Serve the ownership-link disclosure where the intermediary holds 10% or more of the insurer's voting rights or capital, or the insurer holds the same in the intermediary.
Disclose any incentive, contest, override or non-cash benefit tied to the volume or mix of business that could bias the recommendation.
Capture the customer's receipt through DocuSign and record the envelope id and completion timestamp on the Salesforce FSC opportunity before moving to product discussion.
checklist.done: status, remuneration, ownership-link and incentive disclosures are served and receipted with a timestamp preceding any product-specific discussion.

checklist.step: Assemble the product disclosure pack from the matrix, not from memory
actions: Let the system read jurisdiction, product family, channel and advice basis from the opportunity and generate the required document list from the matrix.

Pull each document at its current approved version — key information document or product information document, illustration, contract summary, charges schedule, privacy notice, and any jurisdiction-specific important facts statement.
Stamp every generated document with its version number and generation timestamp in the footer so a later reader can prove what was served.
Block manual substitution of a document from a producer's own files; only system-generated current versions may enter the pack.
Record the assembled list on the opportunity as the pack manifest.
checklist.done: a system-generated pack manifest lists every matrix-required document at its current stamped version, with no manually substituted files.

checklist.step: Deliver the key information or product information document in good time before conclusion
actions: Send the key information document or product information document as its own envelope, separate from the application, so its delivery timestamp stands alone.
Where the customer is not concluding in the same meeting, allow the reflection period the local rule expects and record the elapsed time between delivery and application.
Where the sale concludes in the same session, record the customer's explicit acknowledgement that the document was provided and read before signing, with the timestamp.
Never bundle this document inside the application envelope, since that makes it impossible to show it preceded conclusion.
checklist.done: the key or product information document has its own receipted envelope with a timestamp demonstrably before contract conclusion.

checklist.step: Serve the replacement and exchange notices where an existing contract is affected
actions: Where the Replacement flag is set, generate the jurisdiction's replacement notice and the side-by-side comparison of the existing and proposed contracts.
Populate the comparison with the surrender charge, lost guaranteed benefits, new surrender-charge duration and the computed break-even year from the suitability review.
Serve the notice with the application, obtain both the customer's and the producer's signatures, and record the date each signed.
Where the jurisdiction requires the existing insurer to be notified, generate that notice and record the send date and method.
checklist.done: a signed replacement notice and populated comparison exist dated on or before the application, and any existing-insurer notification is sent and dated.

checklist.step: Serve the privacy notice and capture the consents the notice relies on
actions: Serve the privacy notice covering the categories of personal and health data collected, the purposes, the lawful basis, recipients including reinsurers, cross-border transfers and retention periods.
Capture separately and affirmatively any consent the processing genuinely relies on — health data for underwriting, marketing contact, automated decision-making — never as a pre-ticked box.
Record the notice version, the consent scope and the capture timestamp against the customer record so a later withdrawal can be honoured precisely.
Provide the data subject rights contact details and the supervisory authority the customer may complain to.
checklist.done: the privacy notice version is served and each relied-on consent is separately captured with scope and timestamp against the customer record.

checklist.step: Read the material terms to the customer where the channel is telephone or digital
actions: Follow the approved call script that reads out charges, surrender terms, guarantees and exclusions, and obtain a verbal acknowledgement after each block rather than one at the end.
Confirm the recording is running and tag the call with the application number so the disclosure segment can be retrieved on demand.
For digital self-service journeys, require an affirmative click-through on each material term screen with the screen version and timestamp logged.
Post the full written pack immediately after the call or session and record the send timestamp, since a verbal reading does not replace the document.
checklist.done: the disclosure segment is scripted, acknowledged block by block, recorded and tagged to the application, and the written pack follows with a send timestamp.

checklist.step: Run the pre-submission disclosure gate
actions: Configure the application submit action to validate every document on the pack manifest against a matching receipt with a timestamp on or before its required point.
Block submission — not warn — where any document is missing, superseded or receipted late, and name the failing document in the block message.
Restrict any gate override to the Head of Compliance, require a written reason, and count overrides in the monthly conduct metrics by producer and product.
Write the gate result and the manifest onto the application record so underwriting inherits the evidence.
checklist.done: submission is hard-blocked until every manifest document has an in-time receipt, with overrides restricted, reasoned and counted.

checklist.step: Handle wet-signature, postal and interpreter cases without dropping the proof
actions: For postal or in-person packs, record the despatch date and method and require the customer's dated signature page returned before submission.
Scan returned pages the day they arrive, index them to the application number and record the scan date separately from the signature date.
Where an interpreter or translated pack was used, record the language served, the translation version and the interpreter's name and relationship to the customer.
Treat an undated customer signature as no proof at all and return the pack for re-execution rather than inferring a date.
checklist.done: non-digital packs carry despatch, signature and scan dates, translation details where used, and no undated signature is accepted as proof.

checklist.step: Deliver the contract with the free-look statement and start the clock
actions: Issue the contract with the free-look or cooling-off statement stating the number of days, how to cancel, where to send the cancellation and what will be refunded.
Record the delivery date and method on the policy record and compute the free-look expiry date from delivery, not from issue.
Where delivery is electronic, record the customer's prior consent to electronic delivery and the download or open confirmation.
Set the servicing suppression so no surrender charge or fee can be applied to a cancellation received inside the recorded free-look window.
checklist.done: the contract is delivered with a free-look statement, a delivery-dated expiry is on the policy record, and cancellation inside the window is fee-suppressed.

checklist.step: Version-control disclosure documents and retire superseded ones hard
actions: Publish each new document version with an effective date and simultaneously mark the prior version Retired so it cannot be generated from any template.
Sweep the broker portal, agency shared drives and marketing collateral for retired versions and issue a withdrawal notice to distributors naming the retired version.
Where a version change is material, decide with Regulatory Counsel whether in-flight applications must be re-served on the new version and record the decision.
Keep every retired version in the repository with its effective and retirement dates, since exam questions are always about what was current then.
checklist.done: each version has effective and retirement dates, retired versions cannot be generated, distributors hold a withdrawal notice, and in-flight treatment is decided and recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the served pack and bind it to the policy
actions: File the signed pack, the manifest, envelope ids, completion timestamps and authentication methods, indexed by policy number, application number, producer identifier and jurisdiction.
Apply the 10-years-from-termination retention label and mark packs under complaint or litigation hold as non-purgeable.
Write the repository document id back to the policy record so a complaint handler retrieves the served pack in one hop.
Reconcile archived pack count to issued policy count monthly and chase any policy with no archived pack.
checklist.done: every issued policy has an archived, retention-labelled pack cross-linked to the policy record, reconciled monthly to issued-policy counts.

checklist.step: Remediate a late or missing disclosure at customer level
actions: Open a GRC issue naming the policy, producer, jurisdiction, the missing or late document and the timestamp gap in days.
Re-serve the correct document version to the customer with a covering explanation and record the new receipt.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether to extend the free-look period from the re-service date and whether the failure is reportable to the local conduct regulator, and record both decisions.
Where the same document fails across multiple policies, suspend the affected sales route and sweep the full population for that document before reopening it.
Have the Head of Compliance sign the closure.
checklist.done: each failure is re-served, the free-look and reportability decisions are recorded, systemic failures trigger a route suspension and sweep, and closure is signed.

checklist.step: Feed disclosure failures into complaint and root-cause analysis
actions: Tag every complaint whose root cause is a missing, late or misunderstood disclosure with the specific document and jurisdiction.
Compare the complaint tags to the quarterly test exceptions and report where customers are complaining about documents the test scored as passing — that gap points at content, not delivery.
Refer recurring comprehension complaints to the Marketing Compliance Analyst for a plain-language redraft and to the Learning & Development Specialist for producer coaching.
Report disclosure-driven complaint volumes by document and jurisdiction into the monthly conduct pack.
checklist.done: disclosure-driven complaints are tagged by document and jurisdiction, compared to test results, and routed to content and training owners.

checklist.step: Report the disclosure position to conduct governance
actions: Publish monthly: gate block counts by document, override counts by producer, late-receipt counts, superseded-version incidents and disclosure-driven complaints, all split by jurisdiction.
Present the pack to the Conduct Risk Committee with the remediation status of every open systemic failure.
Escalate any jurisdiction whose matrix has not been re-checked against its governing instrument within 12 months as a compliance risk in its own right.
Minute the committee's decisions on any distribution restriction or regulator self-report.
checklist.done: a monthly disclosure pack by jurisdiction is presented and minuted at the Conduct Risk Committee with open remediation status.

testing.step: Build the population of issued policies and their disclosure records
actions: Extract every life and annuity policy issued in the quarter with application date, issue date, delivery date, jurisdiction, channel, advice basis and producer identifier.
Extract the DocuSign envelope records and document-repository pack manifests for the same period keyed on application number.
Join the two and stratify by jurisdiction, channel, advice basis and replacement flag, recording counts per stratum.
testing.done: a joined, stratified population of issued policies and disclosure records exists with counts recorded per stratum.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the disclosure matrix requirement set
actions: For each stratum, derive independently from the matrix the list of documents that should have been served, rather than accepting the system-generated manifest.
Compare your derived list to the manifest actually generated and list every stratum where the system under-requires a document — a matrix configuration error affects every sale in that stratum.
List every policy with no pack manifest at all, and every manifest with fewer documents than your derived list.
Resolve or list every difference before drawing the sample.
testing.done: an independently derived requirement set is reconciled to the generated manifests, with configuration under-requirements listed at stratum level.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of non-advised digital sales and 100% of sales in any jurisdiction whose disclosure instrument or document version changed during the quarter.
Take 30 further policies at random using a recorded seed, allocated across jurisdictions in proportion to issued volume with a minimum of 5 per active jurisdiction.
Add a judgemental block of every sale where the gate was overridden and every replacement sale.
Record the seed, stratum counts and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and covers all digital non-advised sales, changed jurisdictions, overrides and replacements.

testing.step: Recompute the delivery timing for every sampled document
actions: Pull the envelope completion timestamp for each sampled document and the application, conclusion and delivery timestamps from the policy record.
Compute, per document, the gap in hours between its receipt and its required timing point from the matrix.
List every negative gap — remuneration disclosure after product discussion, key information document after conclusion, replacement notice after application — as an automatic exception.
Confirm the timestamps used are system-generated envelope timestamps and not free-text dates typed by the producer.
testing.done: a per-document timing gap is recomputed for every sampled sale from system timestamps, with every negative gap listed.

testing.step: Verify each served document was the current approved version
actions: Read the version stamp in the footer of each sampled served document and compare it to the version register's current version as at the service date.
List every sale served on a version already retired at the service date, and check whether the retirement was communicated to distributors before that date.
For sales served during a version transition, confirm the in-flight re-service decision recorded by Regulatory Counsel was applied.
Capture the served document footer and the version register entry into the workpaper for each difference.
testing.done: every sampled document's served version is checked against the register as at the service date, with captures for each superseded-version case.

testing.step: Re-read the remuneration and conflicts disclosure text actually served
actions: Read the served text for each sampled sale and confirm it states the nature of the remuneration, not merely that remuneration exists.
Confirm any fee is quantified or its calculation basis given, and that contest, override and non-cash incentive arrangements in force during the quarter are actually named.
Cross-check the served text against the commission plan documents in force at the sale date to confirm nothing material was omitted.
Confirm ownership-link disclosure was served for every intermediary meeting the 10% threshold, using the shareholder register rather than the intermediary's assertion.
testing.done: served remuneration and conflicts text is read against the commission plans and shareholder register in force, with every omission listed.

testing.step: Re-perform the disclosure gate against a deliberately incomplete case
actions: In the test environment, build applications for each jurisdiction and channel with one matrix-required document deliberately unreceipted and attempt submission.
Confirm the submit action hard-blocks and names the failing document, and that the block cannot be cleared by any role other than the Head of Compliance.
Repeat with a receipt timestamped after the required point rather than absent, since a present-but-late receipt is the failure mode a naive gate misses.
Record the result and a capture for each combination and raise any permissive combination as a control design failure.
testing.done: the gate is re-performed for absent and late receipts across every jurisdiction and channel with recorded results and captures.

testing.step: Test the telephone and digital channel disclosure evidence directly
actions: Retrieve the tagged call recording for each sampled telephone sale and listen to the disclosure segment against the approved script.
Confirm charges, surrender terms, guarantees and exclusions were each read and separately acknowledged, and note any block read at speed or skipped.
For digital sales, pull the click-through event log and confirm an affirmative event exists per material term screen with the screen version and timestamp.
Confirm the written pack followed the call or session and list any case where the recording is missing, untagged or overwritten by retention.
testing.done: every sampled telephone and digital sale has its disclosure evidence listened to or event-logged against the approved script, with gaps listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and customer remediation
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming policy, producer, jurisdiction, the document, the timing gap in days and the customer-harm assessment.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — matrix under-configured, version retired late, gate overridden, receipt back-dated, channel evidence missing — and an owner.

Require re-service to the customer and a free-look extension decision within 30 days, and refer any pattern crossing more than 5% of a jurisdiction's sales to Regulatory Counsel for a self-report assessment.
Carry every open exception into next quarter as a mandatory retest row and add the affected jurisdiction to next quarter's 100% coverage list.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a re-service and free-look decision, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the in-time complete-pack rate against the 98% threshold and state separately whether any remuneration or conflicts disclosure was missing and whether any key information document was served after conclusion.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Distribution and Marketing and served no sampled pack, sign the workpaper.
Report the result, the self-report assessments and open remediation to the Conduct Risk Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating the in-time pack rate against the 98% threshold, the zero-tolerance results, a conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly sales supervision programme — the surveillance metric set, the risk-based sampling plan, the file reviews and the corrective-action loop back into Distribution — and reports the results into the Conduct Risk Committee

checklist.step: Cut the quarter's sales population and reconcile it before any analysis
actions: Extract on the 5th business day after quarter end: quotes, applications, issued policies, first-year lapses, surrenders, replacements, free-look cancellations and complaints, each with producer identifier, agency, product code, jurisdiction, premium and dates.
Reconcile issued-policy counts and premium to the policy administration system's quarterly production report and resolve differences before publishing.

Confirm every distribution channel is present — direct, agency, broker, bancassurance, digital and telephone — by comparing channel counts to the prior quarter and investigating any channel that disappeared.
Publish the reconciled dataset with a version stamp so every downstream metric can be traced to one extract.
checklist.done: a version-stamped, reconciled sales dataset covering every channel exists by the 5th business day after quarter end.

checklist.step: Compute the producer surveillance metrics
actions: Compute per producer: replacement rate, first-year lapse rate, free-look cancellation rate, surrender-within-surrender-charge rate, complaints per 1,000 policies, average premium-to-declared-income ratio, and share of sales on the highest-commission product.
Compute concentration metrics: share of sales to customers over 70, share of single-premium business, and share of business in the top product by commission.
Compare each producer to their channel and product peer group and compute a z-score per metric rather than judging against a single company-wide number.
Publish the dashboard with drill-through from the metric to the underlying policy list so a reviewer can see the cases behind a score.
checklist.done: per-producer metrics with peer-relative scores and drill-through to underlying policies are published on the supervision dashboard.

checklist.step: Run the risk-weighting model and build the sampling plan
actions: Load the metric z-scores, prior-quarter findings, tenure, complaint history and product mix into the risk-weighting model and produce a risk score per producer.

Allocate the quarter's review capacity across bands — mandatory full review for the top band, proportionate sampling for the middle, and a random baseline draw across the lowest so no producer has a zero chance of review.
Overlay the ICP 22.3 risk dimensions so high-risk geographies, high-risk product features and third-party introducer channels are over-sampled regardless of producer score.
Record the model version, inputs, weights and the resulting allocation in the sampling plan and have the Compliance Manager approve it before drawing.
checklist.done: an approved sampling plan exists showing model version, weights, band allocation and the risk overlay, with a non-zero draw probability for every producer.

checklist.step: Draw the sample reproducibly and issue the review queue
actions: Draw the sample by the 8th business day using a recorded seed and record population size, band counts and selection date alongside it.
Add mandatory categories in full: every replacement sale to a customer over 70, every sale where the suitability gate was overridden, and every policy that lapsed or was surrendered within 12 months.
Load the drawn cases into the review queue with a reviewer assigned who is independent of the producer's agency and of the original suitability decision.
Publish the queue with the 25th-business-day completion date and daily burn-down reporting.
checklist.done: the sample is drawn from a recorded seed, mandatory categories are included in full, and the queue is loaded with independent reviewers and a completion date.

checklist.step: Review each sampled file against the scoring sheet
actions: Open each case and score the fixed sheet: profile completeness, need-to-product match, horizon and liquidity fit, replacement economics, disclosure timeliness, illustration accuracy, target-market fit and producer training entitlement at the transaction date.
Score each dimension pass, minor finding or material finding, and write the specific evidence reference — field, document, timestamp — behind every non-pass.
Assess customer harm separately from control failure, since a paperwork gap and a wrong product need different responses.
Query the producer through the case system where the file appears incomplete rather than assuming a failure, and record the reply and its date.
Close each file with a reviewer name and date and route material findings straight to the Compliance Manager rather than holding them to the quarter end.
checklist.done: every sampled file has a completed scoring sheet with evidence references behind each non-pass and a separate customer-harm assessment.

checklist.step: Review recorded calls and digital journeys behind sampled sales
actions: Retrieve the recordings tagged to each sampled telephone sale and score the sales conversation for pressure tactics, guarantee overstatement, understated charges and unaddressed customer objections.
For digital journeys, replay the event log and check whether material term screens were dwelt on or clicked through in under the reading time the content requires.
Score the same file dimensions from the call as from the paperwork and report any case where the paperwork passes but the conversation fails — that is the finding that paper-only reviews never catch.
Escalate any call containing a misrepresentation to the Compliance Manager the same day rather than at the end of the review.
checklist.done: every sampled telephone and digital sale is reviewed from the recording or event log, with paperwork-passes-conversation-fails cases reported.

checklist.step: Run mystery shopping on the highest-risk channels
actions: Commission at least 10 shops per quarter targeted at the channels and products the risk model scored highest, using scripted customer profiles including a vulnerable-customer scenario.
Score each shop on whether a fact-find was attempted, whether disclosures were offered unprompted, whether charges were stated accurately and whether the target market was respected.
Debrief findings to the Head of Distribution with the specific producer and agency, and feed the failure modes into the next training cycle.
Never let a shop conclude in an actual sale, and record the withdrawal point for each shop.
checklist.done: at least 10 scored mystery shops covering the highest-risk channels and a vulnerable-customer scenario are completed and debriefed.

checklist.step: Run root-cause analysis on lapses, surrenders and complaints
actions: Take every first-year lapse, in-charge surrender and free-look cancellation in the quarter and code the reason from the customer contact record — affordability, misunderstanding, better alternative, dissatisfaction with charges, or churn by another producer.
Cross-tabulate reason codes by producer, product and channel and identify any cell materially above the portfolio average.
Pull and fully review the files behind any producer or product cell that is an outlier, outside the risk-based sample.
Compare complaint root causes to file review findings and report where customers complain about something the reviews are not catching.
checklist.done: every early lapse, surrender and cancellation is reason-coded and cross-tabulated, with outlier cells fully reviewed outside the sample.

checklist.step: Confirm the findings with the producer and their agency before acting
actions: Send each producer their finding pack with the specific policies, the dimension failed and the evidence reference, and give 10 business days to respond.
Copy the agency principal and, for broker business, the brokerage's own compliance officer.
Downgrade or withdraw any finding the producer disproves with evidence, and record the disproving evidence rather than silently deleting the finding.
Confirm the remaining findings and record the producer's acknowledgement or their disagreement in writing.
checklist.done: every finding is put to the producer and agency with evidence, and each is confirmed, downgraded or withdrawn on the record within the 10-day window.

checklist.step: Apply the corrective-action ladder
actions: Map each confirmed finding to the ladder: coaching note for a first minor finding, mandatory remedial training for repeats, heightened supervision with 100% pre-issue review for material findings, and termination recommendation for misrepresentation or repeated material findings.
Record the action, the owner, the start date and the exit criteria — heightened supervision must state what clean performance ends it, not run indefinitely.
Issue remedial training assignments through the learning management system with a 15-business-day due date and withdraw solicitation entitlement where they are missed.
Escalate every termination recommendation to the Head of Distribution and the Head of Compliance jointly with the finding evidence attached.
checklist.done: each confirmed finding carries a ladder action with an owner, start date and exit criteria, and terminations are jointly escalated with evidence.

checklist.step: Decide and run customer remediation where harm is indicated
actions: Take every file scored as customer harm and decide the remedy with Regulatory Counsel: free-look extension, rescission with full premium return, charge refund, or contract replacement at no cost.
Where a producer or product shows a finding rate above 10%, extend the review to the full population for that segment before deciding remedy scope.
Contact affected customers in writing with a plain explanation, the remedy offered and a response route that does not go through the writing producer.
Record uptake and residual cases and report the remediation programme to the Conduct Risk Committee until it closes.
checklist.done: every harm case has a counsel-agreed remedy, high-finding segments are swept to full population, and affected customers are contacted independently of the producer.

checklist.step: Feed the findings back into product oversight and training
actions: Present the product-level findings — target-market breaches, feature misunderstandings, early lapse concentration — to the Product Oversight Committee as distribution feedback.
Decide per product whether to amend the target market statement, restrict a channel, change a feature, or withdraw the product, and record the decision with an owner and date.
Send the top three failure modes to the Learning Development Manager for the next curriculum version.
Track each product decision to completion in the product backlog so the loop is visibly closed.
checklist.done: product-level findings are presented, a per-product decision with owner and date is recorded, and failure modes are handed to training.

checklist.step: Publish the quarterly supervision report
actions: Write the report by the 30th business day covering population and metrics, sampling methodology and seed, review coverage achieved, finding rates by product, channel and jurisdiction, corrective actions and remediation status.
Compare finding rates to the prior three quarters so trend, not just level, is visible, and state which segments deteriorated.
State plainly where coverage was not achieved and why, rather than reporting only the files that were reviewed.
Have the Head of Compliance sign the report and table it at the next Conduct Risk Committee with the Board Risk Committee receiving the annual roll-up.
checklist.done: a signed quarterly report with methodology, coverage achieved, trended finding rates and remediation status is tabled at the Conduct Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Recalibrate the metrics and the risk model against confirmed findings
actions: Once a year, compare each metric's outlier flags to the findings actually confirmed and compute hit rate and false-positive rate per metric.
Retire metrics that produce no confirmed findings and raise the weight of those that do, recording the evidence for each change.
Re-baseline peer groups where channel mix has shifted, so a producer is not scored against a peer group they no longer resemble.
Approve the recalibrated model version and record it in the sampling plan for the next cycle.
checklist.done: each metric's hit rate is computed annually, weights are adjusted on that evidence, and a versioned recalibrated model is approved for the next cycle.

checklist.step: Archive the cycle evidence for the retention period
actions: File the reconciled extract, metric outputs, sampling plan with model version and seed, completed scoring sheets, call review notes, mystery shop reports, corrective-action records and the signed report.
Index by quarter, producer identifier, product code and jurisdiction so an examiner's request in any of those shapes can be answered directly.
Apply the 7-years-from-report-date retention label and mark cycles inside an open examination as non-purgeable.
Reconcile the archived scoring-sheet count to the drawn sample count and chase any reviewed file with no archived sheet.
checklist.done: the full cycle evidence set is archived, indexed four ways, retention-labelled and reconciled to the drawn sample count.

testing.step: Rebuild the quarter's sales population independently
actions: Re-extract quotes, applications, issued policies, lapses, surrenders, replacements and complaints for the quarter from the warehouse without using the Compliance extract.
Reconcile your counts and premium to the policy administration system production report and to the Compliance dataset, and list every difference.
Confirm every distribution channel and every writing company is present in the Compliance dataset by comparing entity and channel lists.
Record your population and the reconciliation in the workpaper before proceeding.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt population is reconciled to both the administration system and the Compliance dataset, with all differences listed.

testing.step: Re-derive the surveillance metrics from source data
actions: Recompute replacement rate, first-year lapse rate, free-look cancellation rate, complaints per 1,000 and the highest-commission-product share for a block of 20 producers directly from transaction data.
Compare to the published dashboard figures and investigate any difference above a 1 percentage point tolerance.
Check the metric definitions in the procedure against the dashboard's actual query logic, since a definition that drifted silently will move every producer's score.
List any producer excluded from the metric set — new joiners, terminated producers, house accounts — and confirm the exclusion is authorised rather than incidental.
testing.done: metrics are recomputed for 20 producers within tolerance, definitions are checked against query logic, and every exclusion is confirmed authorised.

testing.step: Re-draw the sample and prove the plan was followed
actions: Re-run the risk-weighting model with the recorded version, weights and inputs and confirm the band allocation matches the approved sampling plan.
Re-draw the sample from the recorded seed and compare, case by case, to the sample actually reviewed.

List every case added to or removed from the drawn sample after the draw, and obtain the written reason for each — post-draw substitution is the most common way a supervision programme is quietly softened.
Confirm every mandatory category was taken in full and that no producer had a zero draw probability.
testing.done: the model and draw are reproduced from the recorded version and seed, and every post-draw substitution is listed with its written reason.

testing.step: Re-perform a block of file reviews independently
actions: Select 25 reviewed files weighted toward those scored all-pass, since an ineffective review programme shows up as false passes rather than as missed files.
Score each on a blank sheet before opening the reviewer's sheet, covering the same eight dimensions.
Compare conclusions dimension by dimension and treat any pass you would have scored a material finding as a review-quality exception attributed to the named reviewer.
Test whether reviewers scored the entitlement dimension at the transaction date rather than at review date, a common and invisible error.
testing.done: 25 files are re-scored blind and every false pass is recorded against the named reviewer as a review-quality exception.

testing.step: Verify review coverage was actually achieved inside the cycle
actions: Compare drawn cases to completed scoring sheets and list every drawn case never reviewed or reviewed after the 25th-business-day date.
Check reviewer independence for each completed file — no reviewer inside the producer's agency and none who made the original suitability decision.
Compute the average review duration per file and flag reviewers whose durations are implausibly short against the scoring sheet's length.
Confirm the report's stated coverage figure matches the completed count rather than the drawn count.
testing.done: coverage is verified case by case, reviewer independence is checked per file, and the reported coverage figure is proven against completed reviews.

testing.step: Trace confirmed findings through to corrective actions and their exit criteria
actions: Take every material finding in the cycle and confirm the ladder action applied matches the procedure — no discretionary downgrade without a recorded reason and an approver.
Confirm each heightened-supervision placement states exit criteria and that anyone exited met them, with the evidence attached.
Confirm remedial training assignments were completed inside 15 business days and that entitlement was withdrawn where they were not.
List any finding withdrawn after the producer's response where the disproving evidence is absent from the record.
testing.done: every material finding traces to the correct ladder action with recorded approvals, evidenced exits and completed remedial training.

testing.step: Test the customer remediation actually reached customers
actions: Take every harm-assessed case and confirm the remedy decided by counsel was executed — trace refunds and rescissions to a payment or endorsement transaction in the administration system.
Confirm the customer letter was sent, that it did not route responses through the writing producer, and that non-responders were chased at least once.
Where a segment sweep was triggered by a finding rate above 10%, confirm the sweep covered the full population rather than an enlarged sample.
List any harm case closed with no remedy and read the recorded justification.
testing.done: every harm case traces to an executed remedy transaction and an independently routed customer letter, and every triggered sweep is confirmed full-population.

testing.step: Test whether supervision output actually changed product and training
actions: Take the product-level findings reported in the prior two cycles and trace each to a Product Oversight Committee decision with an owner and date.
Confirm decisions taken have been implemented — target market amended, channel restricted, feature changed — rather than left open across cycles.
Trace the top failure modes to the curriculum version that incorporated them and confirm the version was published and assigned.
List any finding repeated across three consecutive cycles with no product or training change, since that is a broken feedback loop rather than a producer problem.
testing.done: prior-cycle findings are traced to implemented product decisions and published curriculum versions, and repeated unaddressed findings are listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the cycle, the control step, the reviewer or owner involved and the effect on the reliability of the supervision conclusion.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — metric definition drift, post-draw substitution, coverage shortfall, false pass, ladder downgrade without approval, remedy not executed — and an owner in second-line Compliance.
Set a 30-day remediation date and require the next cycle's sampling plan to carry any recalibration the exception demands.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's verification as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, a second-line owner, a 30-day date and a retest commitment in the next cycle.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the verification
actions: State whether the sample was drawn on the approved risk weighting, the coverage percentage achieved against the 100% requirement, the false-pass rate from the blind re-performance, and whether any product or channel exceeded the 10% finding rate without a sweep.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who drew no sample, reviewed no file and set no corrective action in the cycle, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Conduct Risk Committee and the Board Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating coverage, false-pass rate, sweep compliance, a conclusion and both committee reporting dates exists in the repository.
